target_customer: Web service owners and developers who wanted to push alerts to users' phones, plus iPhone users who wanted notifications from any service
problem: Websites had no easy way to send mobile push notifications, and iPhone users could not get alerts from arbitrary services.
business_model: Free consumer app and API for publishers; monetization not established

founders.name: Chad Etzel
founders.background_notes: Joined Twilio after Notifo wound down, per TechCrunch's update citing his blog.

founders.name: Paul Stamatiou
founders.background_notes: Worked on the web app and a GitHub service hook; left for PicPlum before the shutdown. Not listed on the YC page.

exit.reason: TechCrunch reported the team moved on and the service would run only while server costs were covered, with no further development.

competitors.name: Boxcar
competitors.what: $2.99 iPhone app delivering push notifications from Twitter, later opened to other services

competitors.name: Urban Airship
competitors.what: Push notification platform for app developers; first third party push in June 2009

competitors.name: Prowl
competitors.what: Forwarded Growl alerts from desktops to iPhone

technical_complexity.rationale: Relaying through Apple's push service with an API and iPhone client was manageable for two engineers, though reliability at scale needed care.

defensibility.rationale: Apple's push service was open to any developer and rivals shipped the same feature within weeks; no data or network lock-in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Dedicated apps made the relay unnecessary and Boxcar and Urban Airship filled the gap, per TechCrunch in September 2011.

market_need_then: Apple opened push notifications to apps in 2009 and publishers had no simple way to use them, so a generic relay looked useful, but demand stayed thin.

branding.domain_note: notifo.com; the site now shows a coming soon teaser saying Notifo is returning, so the domain is held by a later party.

identity.voice_and_tone: Pitched as a simple mobile notifications platform for anything.

branding.community_and_virality: Covered by TechCrunch and The Next Web at launch; a GitHub service hook gave developer exposure. No evidence of fan culture.

brand_strength.rationale: Early tech press coverage and developer integrations, but the product faded within about two years.

outcome_analysis: Notifo launched in 2010 as a generic push relay and gained early press and some integrations. Dedicated apps made the relay unnecessary while Boxcar and Urban Airship served users and developers, and usage lagged, so the team moved on and TechCrunch reported the shutdown in September 2011. No funding beyond YC is public.
notes: No funding information found beyond the standard YC deal; database sites show empty funding. The notifo.com teaser page is unrelated to the original company as far as sources show. Founded year 2009 is approximate, based on the YC W10 batch.
